title: Regional contingency conductor: staged warm‑standby verification and tier‑aware reroute choreography
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an orchestrated multi-region failover controller that performs progressive warm-standby readiness checks and performs tier‑aware routing adjustments with safe fallbacks to compatible model variants. This ticket captures the control-plane choreography, the gating logic for readiness, the priming sequence for model KV/cache state, and the staged reroute policy that preserves SLOs while minimizing cost impact.

Key behaviors to implement and validate: 1) Readiness gate: combined checks for node health, GPU memory headroom, per-node token throughput, recent KV cache hit ratio, and availability of required model variant (quantized/float) to prevent premature failover. 2) Priming sequence: automated lightweight prime (short sample requests and deterministic prompts) to populate KV caches for hot prefixes before traffic is directed; measure priming throughput and expected latency penalty. 3) Tier‑aware routing: routes are annotated by customer tier (premium/standard/low-cost). During region activation, route weighting shifts progressively (e.g., 10%→30%→60%→100%) with separate backoff curves per tier; premium traffic has accelerated promotion but still honors readiness gating. 4) Model variant fallback: when primary model variant (fp16) is unavailable, orchestrator must identify compatible fallback (int8/q4) and execute a compatibility check (output length, log-prob delta sampling on canary set) before promoting. 5) Circuit breakers & graceful drain: if latency or error budget breaches occur, automatically slow or reverse promotion and trigger warm‑down of newly-activated nodes with eviction plays that preserve in-flight KV entries where possible. 6) Observability: expose per-step metrics (priming success rate, cache_fill_ratio, model_variant_delta, weighted_route_percent) and a concise runbook link.

Non-goals: this ticket does not modify low-level kernel selection heuristics or introduce new model compilation changes — those are separate follow-ups.

Operational notes: the priming sequence must be rate-limited to avoid saturating the warm region; priming requests should be annotated and chargeable to a control budget. All decisions that affect customer‑visible latency must be reversible within 3 minutes.
acceptance_criteria: Controller exposes readiness state with atomic boolean and human-readable failure reasons
Priming run fills KV cache above target hit ratio (>65%) for representative workload within defined priming budget
Tiered promotion logic moves traffic in controlled weights and honors per-tier SLOs; automated rollback on SLO breach verified in chaos tests
Fallback to alternative model variant validated against canary prompts; measured quality delta documented and within tolerated thresholds listed in the runbook
Dashboard widgets show priming progress, per-region headroom, and model-variant health; alerts fire for readiness failures and exceeded priming budget
comments: 2026-02-26 Aisha Patel: Created ticket. Initial RFC attached in attachments. We need a safe default staging plan that minimizes customer impact while exercising cache priming flows.

2026-02-28 Miguel Santos: Architecture review: suggest adding a cheap pre-check for disk-backed KV presence to avoid unnecessary priming when cache snapshot exists. Also propose a 'burst token' bucket for priming to control cost.

2026-03-03 Laura Chen: Design notes: added compatibility matrix for model variants (fp16 -> q4_0, fp32 -> q8_0) and proposed metrics for quality regression (BLEU/ROUGE-like surrogate using sample scoring). See attachment 'compatibility-matrix-v1'.

2026-03-06 Owen Brooks: Engineering update: implemented readiness probe scaffold and a priming worker prototype. Observed priming fill to 45% in early tests; need to increase concurrency safely and add backpressure when node GPU utilization > 70%.

2026-03-10 SRE rotation (Diego Rivera): Ran a simulated region activation during chaos window. The controller correctly halted promotion when model_variant_delta exceeded threshold. Follow-up: tune the delta threshold and add a 'soft-fail' mode for low-cost tier to continue with degraded variant under user-configurable consent.
2026-03-12 Product review (Nina Park): PM approves targeted rollout for internal dev customers next week; requested clearer contract for per-tenant opt-in and a fallback SLA clause.
notes: Testing plan: 1) unit tests for gating logic; 2) integration test using synthetic traffic (latency and token distribution); 3) one canary customer in us-west for pilot; 4) post-mortem template prepared for any degraded rollout. Cost estimate: priming adds ~0.8-1.5% to monthly GPU token cost for active standby depending on workload profile.
